subject: tpa
question: Under Section 5 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, "transfer of property" means an act by which a living person conveys property, in present or in future, to one or more other living persons, or to himself. For this purpose, "living person" includes:
options: only natural persons of full age
the Government alone
only companies registered under the Companies Act
a company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not
explanation: Section 5 defines transfer of property as an act by which a living person conveys property, in present or in future, to one or more other living persons, or to himself and others. Its second paragraph provides that "living person" includes a company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, though nothing in it affects any law relating to transfer of property to or by companies.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, "sale" is a transfer of ownership in exchange for:
options: another property
a periodical payment of rent
love and affection
a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised
explanation: Section 54 defines sale as a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised. A transfer of ownership for another thing is an exchange (Section 118), and a transfer without consideration is a gift (Section 122).

subject: tpa
question: A transfer of a right to enjoy immovable property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions, is defined in Section 105 as a:
options: mortgage
licence
lease
charge
explanation: Section 105 defines a lease of immovable property as a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, for a certain time or in perpetuity, in consideration of a premium or of rent rendered periodically or on specified occasions. A licence, by contrast, creates no interest in the property and is governed by the Indian Easements Act, 1882.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift is the transfer of certain existing movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration, which must be accepted by the donee:
options: within one year of the gift
only after the donor's death
during the lifetime of the donor and while he is still capable of giving
at any time before registration
explanation: Section 122 requires acceptance by or on behalf of the donee during the lifetime of the donor and while he is still capable of giving. If the donee dies before acceptance, the gift is void.

subject: tpa
question: When two persons mutually transfer the ownership of one thing for the ownership of another, neither thing or both things being money only, the transaction is called:
options: an exchange
a sale
a gift
an actionable claim
explanation: Section 118 defines exchange as the mutual transfer of the ownership of one thing for the ownership of another, neither thing or both things being money only. A transfer of property in completion of an exchange can be made only in the manner provided for the transfer of such property by sale.

subject: tpa
question: The doctrine of lis pendens, under which property that is the subject of a pending suit in which a right to it is directly and specifically in question cannot be transferred so as to affect the rights of any other party under the decree, is contained in:
options: Section 41
Section 53
Section 52
Section 53A
explanation: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act embodies lis pendens: during the pendency of a suit or proceeding in which a right to immovable property is directly and specifically in question, the property cannot be transferred or otherwise dealt with by any party so as to affect the rights of any other party under the decree, except under the authority of the court.

subject: tpa
question: The protection given to a transferee who has taken possession of immovable property in part performance of a written contract for transfer is known as the doctrine of part performance and is contained in:
options: Section 53A
Section 52
Section 54
Section 43
explanation: Section 53A, inserted in 1929, bars the transferor from enforcing against a transferee who has taken possession in part performance any right in respect of the property, other than a right expressly provided by the contract's terms. Section 52 deals with lis pendens and Section 43 with feeding the grant by estoppel.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 58(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of:
options: securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability
permanently selling the property
granting a right to enjoy the property for a period
making a gift subject to a condition
explanation: Section 58(a) defines a mortgage as the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability. The transferor is the mortgagor, the transferee the mortgagee, and the instrument the mortgage-deed.

subject: tpa
question: The mortgagor's right, after the principal money has become due, to require the mortgagee on payment or tender of the mortgage-money to return the mortgage-deed and re-transfer the property is called the right of redemption and is contained in:
options: Section 58
Section 67
Section 60
Section 100
explanation: Section 60 confers the right of redemption on the mortgagor once the principal money has become due. Section 67 gives the mortgagee the corresponding rights of foreclosure or sale, and Section 100 deals with charges.

subject: tpa
question: The chance of an heir-apparent succeeding to an estate (spes successionis) is:
options: transferable by a registered instrument
transferable only with the consent of the present owner
transferable after the death of the owner
not transferable under Section 6(a)
explanation: Section 6(a) provides that the chance of an heir-apparent succeeding to an estate, the chance of a relation obtaining a legacy on the death of a kinsman, or any other mere possibility of a like nature, cannot be transferred. Such a chance is not property but a bare expectancy.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, an instrument is "attested" when it has been attested by:
options: one witness who saw the executant sign
the Sub-Registrar at registration
a notary public
two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the executant sign or affix his mark or received his personal acknowledgment of it
explanation: Section 3 defines "attested" as attested by two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the executant sign or affix his mark, or has seen some other person sign in his presence and by his direction, or has received a personal acknowledgment of the signature, and each of whom has signed in the executant's presence. No particular form of attestation is necessary.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift of immovable property must be effected by:
options: delivery of possession alone
an oral declaration before two witnesses
a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses
an unregistered deed signed by the donee
explanation: Section 123 requires a gift of immovable property to be made by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses. A gift of movable property may be made either by such a registered instrument or by delivery.

subject: tpa
question: The rule against perpetuity in the Transfer of Property Act is contained in:
options: Section 14
Section 13
Section 17
Section 18
explanation: Section 14 embodies the rule against perpetuity: no transfer can create an interest taking effect after the lifetime of one or more persons living at the date of the transfer and the minority of some person in existence at the expiry of that period. Section 13 deals with transfers for the benefit of an unborn person, Section 17 with accumulation and Section 18 with transfers for the benefit of the public.

subject: tpa
question: Protection to a transferee who takes property for consideration from a person who, with the express or implied consent of the real owner, appears to be its owner, is given by the doctrine of the ostensible owner under:
options: Section 41
Section 43
Section 48
Section 53
explanation: Section 41 provides that where, with the consent express or implied of the persons interested, a person is the ostensible owner and transfers the property for consideration, the transfer is not voidable on the ground that the transferor was not authorised to make it. The transferee must have taken reasonable care to ascertain that the transferor had power to transfer and acted in good faith.

subject: tpa
question: Where a person fraudulently or erroneously represents that he is authorised to transfer immovable property and transfers it for consideration, the transfer operates on any interest he later acquires in the property, at the transferee's option, under the doctrine of:
options: election
lis pendens
feeding the grant by estoppel
part performance
explanation: Section 43 embodies the doctrine of feeding the grant by estoppel: such a transfer, at the option of the transferee, operates on any interest the transferor subsequently acquires in the property at any time during the subsistence of the contract of transfer. The rights of a good-faith transferee for consideration without notice of that option are protected.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 130 of the Transfer of Property Act, the transfer of an actionable claim, whether with or without consideration, shall be effected only by:
options: the execution of an instrument in writing signed by the transferor or his duly authorised agent
oral agreement and notice to the debtor
delivery of the original debt instrument
an order of the court
explanation: Section 130(1) requires the transfer of an actionable claim to be effected only by an instrument in writing signed by the transferor or his duly authorised agent. On execution, all the transferor's rights and remedies vest in the transferee, whether or not notice of the transfer is given to the debtor.

subject: tpa
question: The modes by which a lease of immovable property determines, such as efflux of time, merger, surrender, forfeiture and expiry of a notice to quit, are listed in:
options: Section 106
Section 108
Section 116
Section 111
explanation: Section 111 lists the modes of determination of a lease: efflux of time, happening of a specified event, termination of the lessor's interest, merger, express or implied surrender, forfeiture and expiration of a notice to determine the lease. Section 106 deals with the duration of leases and notices, and Section 116 with holding over.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 9 of the Transfer of Property Act, a transfer of property may be made without writing:
options: in no case
only in the case of movable property worth less than one hundred rupees
only between members of the same family
in every case in which a writing is not expressly required by law
explanation: Section 9 provides that a transfer of property may be made without writing in every case in which a writing is not expressly required by law. Writing (and usually registration) is required, for example, for sales of tangible immovable property worth one hundred rupees or more (Section 54), mortgages (Section 59), certain leases (Section 107) and gifts of immovable property (Section 123).

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, a sale of tangible immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards can be made:
options: only by a registered instrument
by delivery of the property
by an unregistered sale deed followed by possession
orally, before two witnesses
explanation: Section 54 requires a sale of tangible immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, or of a reversion or other intangible thing, to be made only by a registered instrument. Where the value is less than one hundred rupees, the sale may be made either by a registered instrument or by delivery of the property.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 54, a contract for the sale of immovable property:
options: transfers ownership as soon as it is signed
creates a charge on the property in favour of the buyer
does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property
must always be registered to be valid
explanation: Section 54 provides that a contract for sale is a contract that a sale shall take place on terms settled between the parties, and that it does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property. The buyer's remedy under such a contract is ordinarily a suit for specific performance.

subject: tpa
question: Under the proviso to Section 58(c), a transaction shall not be deemed to be a mortgage by conditional sale unless:
options: the condition is embodied in the document which effects or purports to effect the sale
the mortgagee is put in possession of the property
the principal money exceeds one hundred rupees
the condition is contained in a separate registered agreement
explanation: Section 58(c) describes a mortgage by ostensible sale with a condition that the sale becomes void on payment, or absolute on default. Its proviso requires the condition to be embodied in the very document that effects or purports to effect the sale; a condition in a separate document does not make the transaction a mortgage by conditional sale.

subject: tpa
question: In which kind of mortgage does the mortgagor deliver possession of the property to the mortgagee and authorise him to retain it until payment, receiving the rents and profits in lieu of interest or in payment of the mortgage-money?
options: Simple mortgage
English mortgage
Mortgage by deposit of title-deeds
Usufructuary mortgage
explanation: Section 58(d) defines a usufructuary mortgage as one where the mortgagor delivers possession, or binds himself to deliver it, and authorises the mortgagee to retain possession until payment and to receive the rents and profits in lieu of interest, in payment of the mortgage-money, or partly in each. There is no personal liability of the mortgagor in a pure usufructuary mortgage.

subject: tpa
question: A mortgage by deposit of title-deeds under Section 58(f) (an equitable mortgage):
options: must be by a registered instrument attested by two witnesses
requires delivery of possession of the property
can be created in any village in India by oral agreement
may be created where a person, in a notified town, delivers documents of title to immovable property to a creditor with intent to create a security, and needs no registered instrument
explanation: Section 58(f) recognises a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds where a person in Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai or any town notified by the State Government delivers documents of title to a creditor with intent to create a security. Section 59 expressly excludes this form of mortgage from the requirement of a registered instrument.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 59 of the Transfer of Property Act, where the principal money secured is one hundred rupees or upwards, a mortgage other than a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds can be effected only by:
options: delivery of possession
an unregistered instrument signed by both parties
a registered instrument signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses
an oral agreement recorded before a magistrate
explanation: Section 59 requires a mortgage (other than one by deposit of title-deeds) securing one hundred rupees or more to be effected by a registered instrument signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses. Where the principal money is less than one hundred rupees, a mortgage may be effected either by such an instrument or, except for a simple mortgage, by delivery of the property.

subject: tpa
question: Property is transferred to A on condition that he shall never sell or otherwise dispose of it. Under Section 10 of the Transfer of Property Act, the condition is:
options: void, and A takes the property free of the condition
valid and binding on A
valid only for A's lifetime
voidable at the option of the transferor
explanation: Section 10 makes a condition or limitation absolutely restraining the transferee from parting with or disposing of his interest void, so the transfer stands and the condition falls away. The exception is a lease where the condition is for the benefit of the lessor or those claiming under him; a partial restraint may be valid.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 13 of the Transfer of Property Act, where an interest is created for the benefit of a person not in existence at the date of the transfer, subject to a prior interest created by the same transfer, the interest created for the unborn person:
options: may be a life interest only
takes effect only if the unborn person is a son
is void in all cases
shall not take effect unless it extends to the whole of the remaining interest of the transferor in the property
explanation: Section 13 provides that property cannot be transferred directly to an unborn person, but an interest may be created for him through a prior interest (usually a life estate) in a person living at the date of transfer. The interest for the unborn person must extend to the whole of the transferor's remaining interest, so a life estate to an unborn person is void.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 17 of the Transfer of Property Act, a direction that the income from property shall be accumulated is void, except for permitted purposes, insofar as the accumulation is directed for a period longer than:
options: the life of the transferor, or eighteen years from the date of the transfer
twenty-one years from the date of the transfer
the life of the transferee
the minority of the youngest beneficiary only
explanation: Section 17(1) allows accumulation of income only for the life of the transferor or a period of eighteen years from the date of the transfer; a direction beyond that is void as to the excess. Section 17(2) saves accumulations for payment of debts, raising portions for children or remoter issue, and preservation or maintenance of the property.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 25 of the Transfer of Property Act, an interest created on a condition precedent fails if the fulfilment of the condition is:
options: impossible, forbidden by law, fraudulent, injurious to another, immoral or opposed to public policy
only difficult or expensive
dependent on the will of a third person
to be performed after five years
explanation: Section 25 provides that an interest created on a transfer of property and dependent on a condition fails if the fulfilment of the condition is impossible, forbidden by law, of such a nature that if permitted it would defeat the provisions of any law, fraudulent, involves or implies injury to another, or is immoral or opposed to public policy. The illustrations include conditions requiring a person to kill another or to desert his wife.

subject: tpa
question: Where a person professes to transfer property which he has no right to transfer, and as part of the same transaction confers a benefit on the owner of that property, the owner must either confirm the transfer or dissent from it, and if he dissents, he relinquishes the benefit. This is the doctrine of:
options: lis pendens
marshalling
election
subrogation
explanation: Section 35 embodies the doctrine of election: the owner must elect either to confirm the transfer or to dissent from it, and on dissent the benefit he would have received is relinquished and reverts to the transferor. Election may be express or inferred from conduct, such as accepting the benefit with knowledge of the right to elect.

subject: tpa
question: Under the second paragraph of Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act, where the transferee of a share of a dwelling-house belonging to an undivided family is not a member of the family, he:
options: is not entitled to joint possession or other common or part enjoyment of the house
becomes entitled to joint possession with the other members
may evict the family members after notice
acquires no rights whatever in the share
explanation: Section 44 allows a co-owner to transfer his share, the transferee taking the transferor's rights. But where the share is in a dwelling-house belonging to an undivided family and the transferee is a stranger, he is not entitled to joint possession or other common or part enjoyment of the house; his remedy is to sue for partition.

subject: tpa
question: A person transfers immovable property to B and later purports to create a right in the same property in favour of C, and the two rights cannot coexist in full. Under Section 48, which right prevails?
options: The later right in favour of C, if C paid more consideration
The right that is registered first, regardless of creation
The earlier right in favour of B, subject to any special contract or reservation binding the earlier transferee
The rights are shared equally between B and C
explanation: Section 48 provides that where a person purports to create by successive transfers rights in the same immovable property which cannot all exist or be exercised to their full extent together, each later right shall, in the absence of a special contract or reservation binding the earlier transferees, be subject to the rights previously created. It embodies the maxim qui prior est tempore, potior est jure.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 53(1) of the Transfer of Property Act, a transfer of immovable property made with intent to defeat or delay the creditors of the transferor is:
options: void ab initio
valid against everyone
voidable at the option of any creditor so defeated or delayed
void only if made without consideration
explanation: Section 53(1) makes such a transfer voidable at the option of any creditor so defeated or delayed. It protects the rights of a transferee in good faith and for consideration, and a suit to avoid the transfer must be instituted on behalf of, or for the benefit of, all the creditors.

subject: tpa
question: Where the ownership of the property has passed to the buyer before payment of the whole of the purchase-money, the seller is entitled under Section 55(4)(b) to:
options: rescind the sale without notice
a charge upon the property in the hands of the buyer or any transferee without consideration or with notice of non-payment, for the unpaid price and interest
immediate re-possession of the property
double the unpaid amount as damages
explanation: Section 55(4)(b) gives the unpaid seller a charge upon the property for the amount of the purchase-money unpaid, with interest, against the buyer, any transferee without consideration, and any transferee with notice of the non-payment. The corresponding buyer's charge for price paid in advance is in Section 55(6)(b).

subject: tpa
question: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for a purpose other than agriculture or manufacture is deemed under Section 106 to be a lease from month to month, terminable by either party by:
options: fifteen days' notice
one month's notice ending with the month of the tenancy
six months' notice
three months' notice
explanation: Section 106(1), as amended in 2002, deems such a lease to be from month to month, terminable on the part of either lessor or lessee by fifteen days' notice. Under Section 106(3), a notice is not invalid merely because the period mentioned in it falls short of the specified period, provided the suit or proceeding is filed after expiry of that period.

subject: tpa
question: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed under Section 106 to be a lease:
options: from month to month, terminable by fifteen days' notice
from year to year, terminable by six months' notice
for a fixed period of eleven months
in perpetuity
explanation: Section 106(1) deems a lease for agricultural or manufacturing purposes to be a lease from year to year, terminable on the part of either lessor or lessee by six months' notice. The notice must be in writing, signed by or on behalf of the person giving it, and sent by post, delivered personally or affixed to the property (Section 106(4)).

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, which of the following leases of immovable property can be made only by a registered instrument?
options: A lease from month to month
A lease for six months reserving monthly rent
A lease from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent
Any lease for agricultural purposes
explanation: Section 107 requires a lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent, to be made only by a registered instrument. All other leases may be made either by a registered instrument or by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.

subject: tpa
question: During the subsistence of a lease, the lessee accepts from the lessor a new lease of the same property, to take effect during the continuance of the existing lease. Under Section 111(f), the existing lease determines by:
options: efflux of time
forfeiture
merger
implied surrender
explanation: Section 111(f) provides that a lease determines by implied surrender, and its illustration covers a lessee accepting from the lessor a new lease of the property to take effect during the continuance of the existing lease. Express surrender, by which the lessee yields up his interest to the lessor by mutual agreement, is dealt with in Section 111(e).

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act, if a lessee remains in possession after the determination of the lease and the lessor accepts rent from him or otherwise assents to his continuing in possession, then in the absence of an agreement to the contrary:
options: the lessee becomes a trespasser liable to eviction at once
the lease is renewed from year to year, or from month to month, according to the purpose for which the property is leased, as specified in Section 106
the lease is renewed for the same term as the original lease
the lessee becomes the owner after twelve years
explanation: Section 116 creates a tenancy by holding over where the lessor accepts rent or otherwise assents to the lessee's continued possession after the lease determines. The renewed lease runs from year to year or from month to month according to the purpose of the lease, as specified in Section 106.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 124 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift comprising both existing and future property is:
options: valid as to both
void as to the future property
void as to the existing property
void in its entirety
explanation: Section 124 provides that a gift comprising both existing and future property is void as to the latter. This follows from Section 122, which limits a gift to "certain existing" movable or immovable property.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 126 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift may be suspended or revoked:
options: at the mere will of the donor at any time
on the happening of a specified event, not depending on the will of the donor, if donor and donee have so agreed, or in any case in which it would be rescinded if it were a contract
only by the donee
only with the permission of a court in all cases
explanation: Section 126 allows the donor and donee to agree that a gift shall be suspended or revoked on the happening of a specified event not depending on the donor's will; a gift revocable wholly or partly at the donor's mere will is void to that extent. A gift may also be revoked in any case (except want or failure of consideration) in which, if it were a contract, it might be rescinded.

subject: tpa
question: A gives B, by one instrument, shares in a profitable company X and shares in a company Y which is in difficulties and likely to involve heavy calls. Under Section 127 of the Transfer of Property Act:
options: B may accept the X shares and refuse the Y shares
B cannot accept the X shares without accepting the Y shares
the gift is void in its entirety
B must accept both but may sell the Y shares to A
explanation: Section 127 provides that where a gift is made by a single transfer of several things, of which one is burdened with an obligation and the others are not, the donee can take nothing by the gift unless he accepts it fully. The illustration to the section describes exactly this situation of profitable and burdensome shares.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 129 of the Transfer of Property Act, nothing in Chapter VII (Of Gifts) affects:
options: gifts of immovable property by Hindus
gifts made by companies
gifts of movable property made in contemplation of death (donationes mortis causa) or any rule of Muhammadan law
gifts made to charitable trusts
explanation: Section 129 saves gifts of movable property made in contemplation of death and, save as provided by Section 123, any rule of Muhammadan law. A Muslim gift (hiba) of immovable property may therefore be validly made orally, with declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession, without a registered instrument.

subject: tpa
question: For the purposes of Section 52 (lis pendens), the pendency of a suit or proceeding is deemed to commence from:
options: the date of the cause of action
the date of service of summons on the defendant
the date of presentation of the plaint or institution of the proceeding in a court of competent jurisdiction
the date of framing of issues
explanation: The Explanation to Section 52 provides that pendency commences from the date of presentation of the plaint or institution of the proceeding in a court of competent jurisdiction. It continues until the suit or proceeding has been disposed of by a final decree or order and complete satisfaction or discharge of that decree has been obtained, or has become unobtainable by reason of the expiry of limitation.

subject: tpa
question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for a transferee to claim protection under Section 41 (transfer by ostensible owner)?
options: The ostensible owner held the property with the express or implied consent of the real owner
The transfer was for consideration
The transferee took reasonable care to ascertain that the transferor had power to transfer and acted in good faith
The transfer was made by a registered gift deed
explanation: Section 41 protects a transfer by an ostensible owner only where he holds the property with the consent of the persons interested, the transfer is for consideration, and the transferee, having taken reasonable care to ascertain the transferor's power, acted in good faith. A gift is without consideration and so cannot claim the protection.

subject: tpa
question: Which of the following mortgagees is entitled to sue for foreclosure under Section 67 of the Transfer of Property Act?
options: A simple mortgagee
A usufructuary mortgagee as such
A mortgagee by conditional sale
A mortgagee by deposit of title-deeds, in all cases
explanation: Section 67 gives a mortgagee the right to obtain a decree for foreclosure or sale, but its proviso (clause (a)) permits a suit for foreclosure only by a mortgagee by conditional sale or a mortgagee under an anomalous mortgage whose terms allow it. A simple mortgagee may sue for sale, and a usufructuary mortgagee as such can sue for neither foreclosure nor sale.

subject: tpa
question: Where the owner of two properties mortgages both to one person and then sells one of them to another, the buyer is, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, entitled to have the mortgage-debt satisfied out of the property not sold to him, so far as it will extend. This right, given by Section 56, is called:
options: subrogation
contribution
marshalling by subsequent purchaser
redemption
explanation: Section 56 gives the subsequent purchaser the right of marshalling: to have the mortgage-debt satisfied out of the property not sold to him, so far as it will extend, but not so as to prejudice the rights of the mortgagee or persons claiming under him. Marshalling between mortgagees is in Section 81, and contribution in Section 82.

subject: tpa
question: Property is transferred to A subject to a condition that his interest shall cease if he becomes insolvent or attempts to transfer it. Under Section 12 of the Transfer of Property Act, the condition is:
options: valid and enforceable in all cases
void, except in the case of a lease where the condition is for the benefit of the lessor or those claiming under him
valid only if the transfer is a gift
valid only if registered
explanation: Section 12 makes void a condition or limitation that the transferee's interest shall cease on his insolvency or on his endeavouring to transfer or dispose of it. The exception is a lease, where such a condition for the benefit of the lessor or those claiming under him is valid.

subject: tpa
question: Where immovable property of one person is, by act of parties or operation of law, made security for the payment of money to another, and the transaction does not amount to a mortgage, the latter person has, under Section 100 of the Transfer of Property Act:
options: a lien over the property
a charge on the property
a usufructuary mortgage
an equitable mortgage by deposit of title-deeds
explanation: Section 100 provides that in such a case the person for whose benefit the security is created is said to have a charge on the property, and the provisions applicable to a simple mortgage apply, so far as may be, to the charge. Unlike a mortgage, a charge does not involve a transfer of an interest in the property.

subject: tpa
question: Which of the following is NOT an essential condition for a transferee to claim protection under Section 53A (part performance) of the Transfer of Property Act?
options: The contract to transfer immovable property for consideration is in writing, signed by or on behalf of the transferor
The transferee has taken possession, or being already in possession continues in possession, in part performance of the contract
The transferee has performed or is willing to perform his part of the contract
The transferee has paid the entire consideration before taking possession
explanation: Section 53A requires a written contract signed by or on behalf of the transferor, from which the terms can be ascertained with reasonable certainty; possession taken or continued in part performance; and the transferee having performed or being willing to perform his part. Payment of the entire consideration is not required; willingness to perform suffices.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 14 of the Transfer of Property Act, an interest may take effect after the lifetime of one or more persons living at the date of the transfer only if the ultimate beneficiary:
options: is born within twenty-one years of the transfer
is in existence at the expiry of the lifetime of the last prior life-holder, and the interest vests on his attaining majority at the latest
is a relative of the transferor
attains the age of twenty-five years
explanation: Section 14 limits the vesting of an interest to the lifetime of one or more persons living at the date of the transfer and the minority of some person who shall be in existence at the expiration of that period, and to whom the interest is to belong if he attains full age. Unlike English law, it does not allow a fixed twenty-one-year period; the further period is only the minority of a person then in existence.

subject: tpa
question: Which of the following CAN be transferred under the Transfer of Property Act?
options: A mere right to sue for damages for breach of contract
A right to future maintenance, in whatsoever manner arising
A mere right of re-entry for breach of a condition subsequent, to anyone except the owner of the property affected
An actionable claim, such as a debt due under a contract
explanation: Section 6 bars the transfer of, among others, a mere right of re-entry for breach of a condition subsequent except to the owner of the property affected (clause (b)), a right to future maintenance (clause (dd)) and a mere right to sue (clause (e)). An actionable claim, such as a debt, is property and may be transferred by a written instrument under Section 130.

subject: tpa
question: A mortgage that is not a simple mortgage, a mortgage by conditional sale, a usufructuary mortgage, an English mortgage or a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds is called, under Section 58(g):
options: an equitable mortgage
a charge
a sub-mortgage
an anomalous mortgage
explanation: Section 58(g) defines an anomalous mortgage as a mortgage which is not one of the forms in clauses (b) to (f), for example a combination of a simple and a usufructuary mortgage. The rights of the parties depend on the terms of the deed, including whether the mortgagee may sue for foreclosure under Section 67.

subject: tpa
question: Under the proviso to Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, the mortgagor's right of redemption may be extinguished:
options: by any agreement contained in the mortgage-deed itself
on the expiry of the period fixed for repayment
only by act of the parties or by decree of a court
by the mortgagee's unilateral notice
explanation: The proviso to Section 60 states that the right of redemption subsists unless it has been extinguished by act of the parties or by decree of a court. A term in the mortgage-deed itself that defeats redemption is a clog on the equity of redemption and is void, reflecting the maxim "once a mortgage, always a mortgage".

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 67A of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagee who holds two or more mortgages executed by the same mortgagor, in respect of each of which he has a right to the same kind of decree under Section 67, and who sues on one of them, shall:
options: be free to sue on each mortgage separately in different courts
in the absence of a contract to the contrary, sue on all the mortgages in respect of which the mortgage-money has become due
lose his right on the other mortgages
sue only on the earliest mortgage
explanation: Section 67A requires such a mortgagee, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, to sue on all the mortgages in respect of which the mortgage-money has become due when he sues on any one of them. The provision prevents a multiplicity of suits against the same mortgagor.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 78 of the Transfer of Property Act, a prior mortgagee shall be postponed to a subsequent mortgagee where another person has been induced to advance money on the security of the mortgaged property through the prior mortgagee's:
options: delay in registering the mortgage
fraud, misrepresentation or gross neglect
failure to take possession
acceptance of part payment
explanation: Section 78 postpones a prior mortgagee to a subsequent mortgagee where the subsequent mortgagee was induced to advance money on the security of the property through the fraud, misrepresentation or gross neglect of the prior mortgagee, for example by returning the title-deeds to the mortgagor. It is an exception to the priority rule in Section 48.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 92 of the Transfer of Property Act, a person (other than the mortgagor or a co-mortgagor) who redeems property subject to a mortgage acquires the rights of the mortgagee whose mortgage he redeems. Which of the following is a statutory condition for such subrogation?
options: The mortgage in respect of which the right is claimed must have been redeemed in full
The redeeming person must be a relative of the mortgagor
The subrogation must be ordered by the High Court
The original mortgagee must consent in writing
explanation: Section 92 confers on a person who redeems a prior mortgage the rights of the redeemed mortgagee (legal subrogation), and allows a lender whose money is used to redeem a mortgage to be subrogated by a registered written agreement (conventional subrogation). Its last paragraph provides that no right of subrogation arises unless the mortgage in respect of which it is claimed has been redeemed in full.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 108(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, if the lessor neglects, within a reasonable time after notice, to make repairs which he is bound to make, the lessee may:
options: terminate the lease without notice
make the repairs himself and deduct the expense of such repairs with interest from the rent, or otherwise recover it from the lessor
stop paying rent altogether until the lessor repairs
sublet the property without the lessor's consent
explanation: Section 108(f) allows the lessee, where the lessor neglects to make repairs he is bound to make within a reasonable time after notice, to make them himself and deduct the expense with interest from the rent or otherwise recover it from the lessor. The rights and liabilities in Section 108 apply in the absence of a contract or local usage to the contrary.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act, where a lease has been determined by forfeiture for non-payment of rent and the lessor sues to eject the lessee, the court may relieve the lessee against the forfeiture if, at the hearing of the suit, the lessee:
options: promises in writing to pay the rent within six months
pays or tenders the rent in arrear, with interest and the full costs of the suit, or gives security for payment within fifteen days
files a counter-claim for repairs
shows that he has been in possession for more than twelve years
explanation: Section 114 empowers the court to pass an order relieving the lessee against forfeiture for non-payment of rent if, at the hearing, he pays or tenders to the lessor the rent in arrear, with interest and the full costs of the suit, or gives such security as the court thinks sufficient for making these payments within fifteen days. Relief against forfeiture on other grounds is governed by Section 114A.

subject: tpa
question: A transfers property to B absolutely, with a direction that B shall live in a particular house and not let it out. Under Section 11 of the Transfer of Property Act:
options: the direction is binding on B, and breach forfeits the property
B takes the interest as if there were no such direction
the whole transfer is void
the direction converts B's interest into a life interest
explanation: Section 11 provides that where an interest is created absolutely in favour of a person but the transfer directs that it shall be applied or enjoyed in a particular manner, he is entitled to receive and dispose of the interest as if there were no such direction. The exception is a direction regarding one piece of immovable property for the beneficial enjoyment of another piece of the transferor's property.

subject: tpa
question: Under Section 136 of the Transfer of Property Act, which of the following persons shall NOT buy, traffic in, stipulate for or agree to receive any share of or interest in an actionable claim?
options: A bank officer
A judge, legal practitioner or officer connected with any court of justice
A company director
A government servant in the revenue department
explanation: Section 136 bars any judge, legal practitioner or officer connected with any court of justice from buying, trafficking in, stipulating for or agreeing to receive any share of or interest in any actionable claim. No court shall enforce, at his instance or that of any person claiming through him, an actionable claim so dealt with.
